sources.title: Teul (Wikipedia)
sources.usedFor: The list of 24 patterns, the historical periods they belong to, the history of how the patterns were created, and General Choi's nine practice points.

sources.title: Namesake articles (Wikipedia)
sources.usedFor: A two-sentence excerpt about the person or idea each pattern is named after. Each excerpt is shortened from the article lead and shown with a link to its article, its edit history and the revision it was taken from. See the list below.

sources.title: ITF patterns
sources.license: No licence stated; facts only, paraphrased
sources.usedFor: A cross-check of movement counts, the rank each pattern is taught at, and the one-line meaning of each pattern. Facts are not copyrightable; no wording is copied.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Taekwon-Do (1999)
sources.publisher: General Choi Hong Hi, International Taekwon-Do Federation
sources.license: Copyright the author; cited, not reproduced
sources.usedFor: The canonical authority for the patterns, named by Wikipedia as the reference for how every pattern is performed. Its movement sequences are copyrighted and are not included here.

sources.title: ITFtuls on YouTube
sources.license: Copyright the uploader; embedded through YouTube's player, not copied
sources.usedFor: One demonstration video for each of the 24 patterns. Videos load only when you press play, through youtube-nocookie.com, and every video was confirmed embeddable through YouTube's oEmbed endpoint.

sources.title: TITF Black Belt Registry: Verify Ranks
sources.usedFor: Verifies the instructor credential shown on the About page: Mr. Lawrence Jefferson, USA, 7th Degree, International Master Instructor.

sources.title: Valspar Cottage Blue (209D)
sources.usedFor: The starting colour of the Blue Cottage theme, #83a8ca. The rest of the palette is derived from it.

discrepancies: itftaekwondo.com/patterns lists Tong-Il with 42 movements and Choi-Yong with 45. This app uses 56 and 46, the standard ITF counts, as recorded in the TITF handbook this project was first built from.

That page says there are 24 patterns but names 25, because it lists both Ko-Dang and Juche. This app follows Wikipedia's Teul: 24 current patterns including Juche, with Ko-Dang shown separately as a former pattern.

Wikipedia gives no per-pattern movement counts or belt grades. Those come from the ITF syllabus and the cross-check above, not from a free-licensed document, so treat them as facts to confirm with your instructor.
